The risk assessment includes evaluating financial risks, operational risks, and compliance risks, which can be done in any order but must all be completed.
If high risk is identified, then a detailed investigation is launched.
The investigation includes data analysis, interviews, and, in certain cases, site visits.
After all risks are addressed, the audit team compiles the audit report.
The report is reviewed by the audit director.
The audit director may approve the report or send it back for revisions.
If revisions are required, the audit team updates the report accordingly and resubmits it to be reviewed again by the audit director.
Once approved, the final report is distributed to the executive board and archived.
The entire audit process is then closed.

args.text: When the process description states an activity, label the BPMN activity with a concise action and object that faithfully represents the described action; do not substitute a related but different activity.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already addresses faithful activity labeling.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Return one complete, well-formed bpmn:definitions document and no surrounding explanation or Markdown fence.

args.text: When the description states an activity or event, label the BPMN element with a concise, faithful name that represents its actual action or meaning; do not use a related but different action.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers faithful labeling.

result.rule: When the description states a specific business trigger or process outcome for a start or end event: Label the corresponding BPMN event with a concise phrase that preserves that stated trigger or outcome, rather than using a generic label such as “start” or “end”.

When the description names an activity or outcome with multiple stated actions, alternatives, or a distinguishing object or participant.: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or event so its described scope remains identifiable. Preserve materially stated actions, alternatives, and objects or participants; do not substitute a broader or different action or add unsupported details.

When the description gives contextual details or examples alongside a single activity, without presenting them as separate actions: label the BPMN task with its core action and object; omit contextual details and qualifiers that are not needed to identify the activity

When the description states a core activity and separately describes a condition or later outcome that marks its completion: Label the BPMN activity with its core action and object; do not add the separately stated completion condition or later outcome to the activity label.
